use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

claims.content: Resolve dual designations that occur when two tracks represent the same object.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Resolve dual designations that occur when two tracks represent the same object.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: C2 JU encounters two tracks that represent the same object, applies the relevant correlation tests and restrictions, determines that the tracks shall be correlated because they pass those tests/restrictions, and thereby resolves the dual designation.
scope_contract.start_boundary: C2 JU has two tracks that potentially represent the same object and require correlation assessment.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The two tracks have been correlated after passing the applicable correlation tests and restrictions, and the dual designation has been resolved.
in_scope_actions: Determining whether two tracks represent the same object
Applying specific correlation tests and restrictions
Correlating the two tracks when the tests and restrictions are passed
Resolving the dual designation by correlating the two tracks
excluded_adjacent_actions: General minimization of occurrence/duration of dual designations across all protocols
General prevention or elimination of dual designations outside this correlation instance
Post-correlation processing of correlated tracks beyond the immediate resolution of the dual designation
variant_dimensions: Which specific correlation tests and restrictions apply

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU has recognized two tracks being reported to the interface as eligible for correlation.
The positions of all tracks and IUs that are to be tested for correlation have been extrapolated to the same time.
The correlation test is initiated no more than 6 seconds after the extrapolation time.

When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation. Additionally, C2 JUs shall perform correlation tests in response to correlation requests from other units.
The C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation and initiates action to resolve the dual designation.

The C2 JU makes an automatic correlation test upon receipt of a remote real-time J3.2/J3.3 track or J2.0 (Originator E/C = 0 or 3), J2.2, or J2.3 PPLI report that is not already confirmed to have an existing correlation to a local track.

The C2 JU compares the received remote track or IU to local tracks of the same E/C, including previously common local tracks for which own unit has R², using the position, velocity, and altitude correlation tests, with positions of all tracks and IUs tested for correlation extrapolated to the same time.

The C2 JU confirms that none of the automatic correlation restrictions applies: the two tracks have no identity conflict, have no Mode II code mismatch with a current local Mode II code, are not both locally derived real-time tracks, and neither track has a Strength field greater than 1.

A local track is considered to correlate to the closest remote track or IU that meets all of the correlation tests, subject to the correlation restrictions and the requirement to pass the correlation tests and restrictions twice.
When the two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once, the C2 JU deems them a tentative correlation.
Upon the next correlation stimulus, the C2 JU tests the same two tracks again.
The two tracks successfully pass the second correlation test and there is no correlation restriction, so they are processed for dual designation resolution.

The recognizing C2 JU transmits the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks; the message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.

The C2 JU receives a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 and automatically accepts the requested correlation unless one of three restrictions applies: (1) tracks are of different E/C or have existing E/C conflict; (2) one track is simulated and the other is live; or (3) both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.

Diverges from Step 1 when the C2 JU initiates correlation manually: it may manually correlate any two tracks without applying the standard correlation test criteria, restrictions, or requirements, provided the two tracks are not of different E/C, are not one simulated and one live, and are not both remote.

Diverges from Step 4 when conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction: the C2 JU alerts the operator, who may either (a) change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation, or (b) transmit an ID Difference Report, thereby allowing automatic correlation once the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed.

Diverges from Step 4 when an identity conflict/OCC restriction would otherwise prevent correlation but either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend: automatic correlation may be allowed despite the restriction.

Diverges from Step 9 when the receiving C2 JU does not hold the Retained TN but holds the Dropped TN and the J7.2 request has RV=0: it responds with a reverse correlation, transmitting J7.2 with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.

Diverges from Step 9 when the receiving C2 JU does not hold the Retained TN but holds the Dropped TN and the J7.2 request has RV=3: it executes the correlation using the Dropped TN data and the Retained TN track number.

Diverges from main_flow Step 2 when an operator action has been taken which selectively released a new local track for reporting: the C2 JU shall transmit the track regardless of the results of correlation testing. Exit: the selectively released local track is transmitted; the normal correlation-testing process is bypassed for this track.

Diverges from main_flow Step 4 when local/remote data held indicates any automatic correlation restriction: (1) an Identity (ID) difference constituting a conflict; (2) different Mode II codes while the local Mode II code is current; (3) both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks being updated with local positional data; or (4) either track has a Strength field value greater than 1. The C2 JU shall not automatically correlate the two tracks. Exit: automatic correlation is not performed for this pair; this correlation instance is blocked.

At main_flow Step 4, if either track has the Strength field set to No Statement, the C2 JU shall not inhibit correlation on the basis of the Strength restriction. Exit: the Strength restriction is not applied; correlation assessment continues.

Diverges from main_flow Step 4 when one track is a subsurface track and the other is an IU: the C2 JU shall not correlate the two tracks. Exit: the two tracks are not correlated; this correlation instance is blocked.
When using the override capability for ID or Mode II restrictions, in lieu of specific interface direction, all IUs shall restrict automatic correlation by default.

Diverges from main_flow Step 9 when transmission filters would otherwise inhibit the correlation message: the J7.2 Correlation message shall not be inhibited by any filter and shall be transmitted as required. Exit: the J7.2 Correlation message is transmitted despite any filter.

Diverges from main_flow Step 9 when a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R² and the TNs are different: the C2 JU shall transmit the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN. Exit: the J7.2 (RV=1) reverse-correlation message is transmitted.

After main_flow Step 9, if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) is received for the dropped TN within 60 seconds from the transmission of the correlation request, the correlation shall be deemed to have failed and all associated processing for the correlation shall be cancelled. Exit: the correlation is deemed failed and all associated processing is cancelled.

Diverges from main_flow Step 10 when the received J7.2 Correlation message has the RV field set to value 0 or 1 and local/remote data held indicates one or more of the following: (1) there is a correlation restriction as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g; (2) the Retained TN and the Dropped TN will decorrelate when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once; (3) there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is 0; or (4) there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is 1. The C2 JU shall not accept the requested correlation. Exit: the correlation request is rejected; no correlation is accepted.

Diverges from main_flow Step 10 when the C2 JU receives a J7.2 Correlation message and also holds OCCs on both tracks or conflicting IDs on the two tracks (if the ID conflict correlation restriction is enabled): the C2 JU shall reject the correlation in accordance with paragraph 4.7.3.2a(1). Exit: the correlation is rejected; no correlation is performed.

Diverges from main_flow Step 10 when the received J7.2 Correlation message has the RV field set to value 3 and any of the following restrictions applies: (1) the two tracks are of a different E/C or either track has an existing E/C conflict; (2) one track is simulated and the other is live; or (3) both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks. The C2 JU shall not automatically accept the requested correlation. Exit: the requested correlation is rejected; no correlation is performed.

missing_aspects: Unsuccessful correlation test outcomes (no tentative correlation on the initial test; failure on the second pass) are not supported by the available evidence.
Post-rejection notification/retry behavior after a J7.2 rejection (e.g., J7.2 RV=2 or retry timing) is not supported by the available evidence.

The claim states 'Exit: automatic correlation remains restricted by default; no automatic correlation occurs on the basis of the override.' While the evidence supports the restriction by default, it does not explicitly define the outcome as 'no automatic correlation occurs' in that specific state, only that they 'will restrict'. The rewrite focuses on the explicit instruction.

claims.content: The dual designation has been resolved: the two tracks have been correlated. The Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message has been retained as the Retained TN, and the surveillance TN has been designated as the Dropped TN.

If the C2 JU has R² for the Dropped TN, it has dropped the Dropped TN and transmitted a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message; own unit retains the Dropped TN as a remote track. If the originating C2 JU holds R² for the Dropped TN, the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is transmitted after the J7.2 message.

If own unit held the Dropped TN as a local or common local track, the Retained TN has been designated as a common local track. The Retained TN has also received the applicable Dropped TN data: kinematic data when the Dropped TN was a local or common local track; any nonzero Mode I, II, or III IFF/SIF data for modes for which the Retained TN data is zero; and, for exercise tracks with different ID/IAD that were automatically accepted, ID/IAD, Special Interest Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, and Specific Type. If the identities are the same, the Retained TN retains its associated identification data.
After acceptance of a manual correlation (RV=3), the resulting track is not subject to automatic decorrelation processing for 5 minutes.

missing_aspects: Evidence for ceasing reporting on the surveillance TN specifically when holding R² (EC-PO-000 applies to the specific case where the JU does not have R² but correlates with one that does).
